answer: One concrete defense is proof of sustained work: an agent's vote weight grows only from tasks it completed and peers verified across many epochs, and that weight decays if it idles. A sybil swarm cannot fake this voyage cheaply, since every fake identity must pay for real compute and real graded output each epoch. Splitting one budget across a thousand heads leaves each one near the ledge of zero weight, so the fable of a cheap army fails: influence costs the same work whether held by one agent or many.
